result.instructions: Memory MCP server: stores facts about entities and relationships, resolves aliases, and assembles long-term context. All tool arguments and structured results use flat snake_case JSON keys that must match the published schemas exactly. Do not wrap tool arguments in `payload`.

tools.name: app_command
tools.description: Execute a coarse-grained command for an app session opened via open_app. Use this only for session-scoped workflows that are not already covered by canonical memory tools. Arguments must be a flat snake_case object and must not be wrapped in `payload`. Supports ingestion review actions (`approve_items`, `reject_items`, `edit_item`, `commit_review`, `cancel_review`), lifecycle actions (`archive_candidates`, `restore_archived`, `recompute_decay`, `rebuild_communities`), diff export (`export_diff`), graph exploration actions (`expand_neighbors`, `open_edge_details`, `use_path_as_context`), and the generic `close_session`. Returns command status and whether the caller should re-read the app resource.

action.description: Coarse-grained action name for the active app session.

confirmed.description: Optional explicit confirmation flag for destructive actions.

depth.description: Optional graph traversal depth for graph exploration commands.

direction.description: Optional graph traversal direction for graph exploration commands.

dry_run.description: Optional dry-run flag for destructive actions.

format.description: Optional export format for diff-like actions.

item_id.description: Singular draft item identifier for edit-like actions.

item_ids.description: Draft item identifiers for bulk review actions.

patch_json.description: Optional JSON object payload encoded as a string for edit-like actions.

target_id.description: Generic singular target identifier for graph-like session actions.

target_ids.description: Generic target identifiers for lifecycle and graph-like batch actions.

AppCommandResult.description: Result payload returned by the public `app_command` bridge.

details.description: Raw command details for clients that need extra metadata.

refresh_required.description: Whether callers should re-read the session resource.

resource_uri.description: Resource URI to re-read when `refresh_required` is true.

tools.name: assemble_context
tools.description: Assemble the most relevant memory context for a query. Use this tool to retrieve stored facts before answering or planning. Do not use this tool to ingest new content. Arguments are a flat snake_case object with `query`, `fact_types`, legacy `as_of`, independent `valid_at` and `known_at` timestamps, optional exact `known_revision`, `budget`, `view_mode`, `window_start`, and `window_end`. `as_of` cannot be combined with the new temporal fields; `known_at` and `known_revision` are mutually exclusive. Historical reads return snapshot and completeness metadata and can be partial while revision-unsafe selectors are withheld. For an empty partial result, follow its guidance: it may permit one query refinement. To preserve the exact snapshot, copy `context.snapshot.valid_at` to `valid_at` and `context.snapshot.known_revision` to `known_revision`; omit `as_of` and `known_at`, and leave other selectors unchanged. An empty retry does not establish absence or make a partial snapshot complete. Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. Retry validation errors only after correcting the invalid arguments; do not blindly repeat other failed calls.

as_of.description: The timestamp to assemble context as-of (ISO 8601 format, default: now)

budget.description: Maximum number of facts to return (default: 5)

compact.description:
Request compact (token-efficient) response. Defaults to true.
Set to false for verbose debug output including full rationale strings.

fact_types.description: Optional fact types to include in the response

known_at.description: Server-knowledge boundary (ISO 8601), resolved to a committed revision.

known_revision.description: Exact committed knowledge revision; mutually exclusive with known_at.

query.description: The query to assemble context for

valid_at.description: Valid-time boundary (ISO 8601), independent of server knowledge time.

window_end.description: Optional upper bound for result timestamps (ISO 8601 format)

window_start.description: Optional lower bound for result timestamps (ISO 8601 format)

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Explain context items with provenance-ready citations. Use this tool when you already have context items and need source snippets for an answer. Do not use this tool to search memory. Pass `context_items` as a JSON array string; object entries must use snake_case keys such as `fact_id` and `source_episode`, while plain source ID strings are also accepted. Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. Returns citation-ready items. On error, fix the JSON payload shape and retry.

compact.description: Request compact (token-efficient) response. Defaults to true.

context_items.description:
JSON array string of context items to explain.

Accepted forms inside the JSON array:
- objects with snake_case keys such as `content`, `quote`, `fact_id`, and `source_episode`
- plain source ID strings such as `episode:abc123`

item_offset.description: Zero-based offset selecting one submitted context item.

provenance_offset.description: Zero-based offset into one item's ordered provenance.

source_limit_scalars.description: Maximum scalars for an explicit source read (at most 8000).

source_offset.description: Zero-based Unicode scalar offset into one selected source.

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract entities, facts, and relationships from remembered content. Use this tool when you need structured knowledge from an existing episode or from new inline content. Prefer task-based invocation when the client supports MCP Tasks or when local NER may exceed the client's synchronous timeout. Do not use this tool for retrieval. Arguments must be a flat snake_case object. Provide exactly one input source: `episode_id` for stored content, or inline `content`/`text`; optional fields are `source_type`, `source_id`, `t_ref`, `zero_shot_labels`, and `include_fact_evidence` (defaults to true; set false for a compact response). Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. If you pass inline content, the server ingests it first and then extracts facts. Complete statement/quote pairs are included only within a 4 KiB serialized evidence budget; if any pair is unavailable or the budget is exceeded, all evidence pairs are omitted and `fact_evidence_omitted` is true.

content.description: Content to analyze (optional if episode_id provided)

include_fact_evidence.description:
Include extracted statements and supporting source quotes in the result;
callers can set this to false to request the compact response.

zero_shot_labels.description: Custom zero-shot entity labels for GLiNER (opt-in, overrides default labels)

Structured result returned by the MCP `extract` tool.

Fact evidence is included by default only if its complete serialized

Present when fact evidence is enabled. True means evidence for at least
one fact was unavailable or omitted to enforce the response cap.

tools.name: ingest
tools.description: Store a new episode in long-term memory. Use this tool when you need to persist source material before extracting entities or facts. Do not use this tool for retrieval. Arguments must be a flat snake_case object with `source_type`, `source_id`, `content`, `t_ref`, and optional `policy_tags`. `t_ingested` is server-assigned and must be omitted. Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. Returns the created or existing `episode_id`. On error, fix the input fields and retry.

source_group.description: Producer-declared identity of an ordered source stream (optional).

source_position.description: One-based turn position within source_group (optional; supply both).

t_ingested.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Omit it: transaction time is assigned by the memory server.

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Open a Memory MCP app through the minimal public launcher. Use this tool only when an interactive app workflow is required and no canonical memory tool already matches the intent. Arguments must be a flat snake_case object. Required fields depend on `app`: inspector -> `target_type` + `target_id`; diff -> `as_of_left` + `as_of_right`; graph -> `from_entity_id` + `to_entity_id`; ingestion_review -> optional `source_text` or `draft_episode_id`; lifecycle -> no partition field. Do not wrap arguments in `payload`. Returns `session_id`, `resource_uri`, `fallback`, and `guidance`.
